gloss: trust, rely on; be secure, unafraid; security
summary: To lean one's weight on someone or something and so be without fear: to trust in, and, with no object, to be secure, at ease. Scripture sets trust in Yahweh against trust in man, wealth, walls, idols or one's own righteousness, and its opposites are fear and being put to shame: “I will trust and not be afraid” (Isa 12:2), “in you they trusted and were not ashamed” (Psa 22:6). The noun בֶּטַח is security, above all Israel dwelling לָבֶטַח “in security” in the land Yahweh gives them, now promised and in the latter days to be fulfilled; it is also the false ease of a people off guard. The Aramaic of the Targums uses the same root for trust, and the Punic shows it too; the one-word “watermelons” of Num 11:5 is a separate word in the same spelling.

words.gloss: trust, rely on; be secure, confident; (hiphil) make to trust
words.summary: About 120 times, almost all qal. With בְּ, עַל or אֶל it is to trust in, rely on, lean on (Isa 50:10, “let him trust in the name of Yahweh and lean on his God”); with no object it is to be secure, confident, without fear, rightly or wrongly. The passive participle בָּטוּחַ “trusting, steadfast” (Isa 26:3; Psa 112:7) is counted here.

stems.gloss: trust in, rely on; be secure, confident, unafraid

senses.definition: To put one's weight and hope on a person or thing, expecting help or safety from it. The object decides the outcome: one who trusts in Yahweh is not put to shame; one who trusts in man, riches, fortifications, idols or false words falls with what he leaned on.

evidence.note: “Cursed is the man who trusts in man (אֲשֶׁר יִבְטַח בָּאָדָם) and makes flesh his arm, and whose heart turns from Yahweh … Blessed is the man who trusts in Yahweh, and Yahweh is his מִבְטָח”: the two objects of trust set side by side, the shrub in the desert and the tree by the waters.
“Let him trust (יִבְטַח) in the name of Yahweh and lean (וְיִשָּׁעֵן) on his God”: trust is leaning one's weight.
“Better to take refuge (לַחֲסוֹת) in Yahweh than to trust (מִבְּטֹחַ) in man … than to trust in princes.”
“In you our fathers trusted; they trusted, and you delivered them … in you they trusted and were not ashamed (וְלֹא־בוֹשׁוּ).”
“Trust in Yahweh with all your heart, and do not lean (אַל־תִּשָּׁעֵן) on your own understanding.”
“In God I have trusted; I will not fear. What can flesh do to me?”
“Trust in Yahweh and do good; dwell in the land.”
“Roll your way upon Yahweh, and trust in him, and he will act.”
“Do not trust in princes, in a son of man, in whom there is no salvation”: for his breath goes out and he returns to his earth (v. 4).
“Those who trust in their wealth and boast in the abundance of their riches”: none can redeem his brother from death (v. 8).
“He who trusts in his riches will fall.”
“Your high and fortified walls in which you trusted.”
Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help, who lean on horses “and trust in chariots … but do not look to the Holy One of Israel”.
The maker of an idol “trusts in his own work” to make dumb idols.
“Do not trust in lying words, saying, The temple of Yahweh, the temple of Yahweh.”
“If he trusts in his own righteousness (וְהוּא־בָטַח עַל־צִדְקָתוֹ) and does iniquity, none of his righteousness shall be remembered.”
“You trusted in your beauty and played the harlot.”
Hezekiah “trusted in Yahweh the God of Israel”.
The Rabshakeh's taunt, built on the word: “What is this confidence in which you trust? … On whom do you trust, that you have rebelled against me? … you trust in the staff of this broken reed, Egypt.”
God answered the tribes in battle “because they trusted in him”.
“Trust in him at all times, you people; pour out your heart before him.”
“Do not trust in oppression, and do not become vain in robbery.”
Of the wild ox: “Will you trust him because his strength is great?”
“Do not trust in a friend; do not rely on a companion.”

senses.definition: With no object: to be at ease and unafraid. Of the righteous, a settled confidence that does not fear (Pro 28:1); of a people or a city, ease that has no thought of danger, often with שָׁקַט “quiet” and שַׁאֲנָן “at ease”, and often just before ruin.

evidence.note: Laish was “quiet and secure (שֹׁקֵט וּבֹטֵחַ)”, far from the Sidonians, with no dealings with anyone.
Dan came “upon a people quiet and secure” and struck them.
“You will come to a secure people (עַם בֹּטֵחַ).”
“Women at ease (שַׁאֲנַנּוֹת) … daughters בֹּטְחוֹת”: complacent; within a year they will tremble.
“The wicked flee when no one pursues, but the righteous are confident (יִבְטָח) like a young lion”: the opposite of fleeing in fear.
“Behold, God is my salvation; I will trust and not be afraid (אֶבְטַח וְלֹא אֶפְחָד).”
“Though a camp encamps against me, my heart will not fear; though war rises against me, in this I am confident.”
“The wise fears and turns from evil, but the fool is arrogant and confident (וּבוֹטֵחַ).”
Behemoth: “if the river rages he is not alarmed; he is confident (יִבְטַח) though the Jordan bursts against his mouth.”
“You will be secure (וּבָטַחְתָּ), because there is hope; you will look about and lie down in security (לָבֶטַח).”
The caravans “were ashamed because they had been confident; they came there and were confounded”.
“If in a land of peace you are secure, how will you do in the thicket of the Jordan?”
“Woe to those at ease in Zion and those secure (וְהַבֹּטְחִים) on the mountain of Samaria.”
“You keep him in perfect peace whose mind is stayed on you, because he trusts (בָּטוּחַ) in you.”
“He will not fear an evil report; his heart is firm, trusting (בָּטֻחַ) in Yahweh.”

senses.definition: To lead another to trust: of Hezekiah urging the people to trust in Yahweh, of false prophets making the people trust in a lie, and of Yahweh keeping the infant safe and trusting at the breast.

evidence.note: “Do not let Hezekiah make you trust (יַבְטַח) in Yahweh, saying, Yahweh will surely deliver us.”
“Yahweh has not sent you, and you have made this people trust in a lie (הִבְטַחְתָּ … עַל־שָׁקֶר).”
Shemaiah “made you trust in a lie”.
“You are he who drew me from the womb, מַבְטִיחִי upon my mother's breasts”: who made me trust, or kept me secure.

evidence.locator: Psa.118.8 → πεποιθέναι; Psa.146.3 → πεποίθατε; Pro.11.28; Isa.12.2; Isa.36.4 → πεποιθώς; Ezk.33.13 → πέποιθεν; Jer.7.4 → πεποίθατε; πείθω renders בָּטַח ×49

evidence.note: “Some who trusted in themselves (πεποιθότας ἐφ᾽ ἑαυτοῖς) that they were righteous”: the trust in one's own righteousness of Ezk 33:13.
“That we should not trust (πεποιθότες) in ourselves, but in God who raises the dead.”
“I will put my trust in him (ἔσομαι πεποιθὼς ἐπ᾽ αὐτῷ)”: the Septuagint's words for Isa 12:2 אֶבְטַח, and for Isa 8:17, the verse whose next words Hebrews goes on to quote.
“He trusted (πέποιθεν) in God; let him deliver him now”: the mockers of Psa 22, where the fathers “trusted and you delivered them” (Psa 22:5).

evidence.locator: Psa.22.5 → ἤλπισαν; Psa.112.7 → ἐλπίζειν; ἐλπίζω renders בָּטַח ×28

evidence.note: Charge the rich “not to set their hope (ἠλπικέναι) on the uncertainty of riches, but on God”: the trust in wealth of Psa 49:7 and Pro 11:28.

parallels.note: Take refuge: “better to take refuge in Yahweh than to trust in man”.
Lean on: trust is leaning one's weight on someone.
Be quiet, undisturbed: the secure people of Laish.

opposites.note: Be ashamed, disappointed: what trust escapes, or what false trust ends in.
Be in dread: “I will trust and not be afraid”.
Fear: “in God I have trusted; I will not fear”; the fear of man against trusting Yahweh.

words.summary: Mostly adverbial, לָבֶטַח or בֶּטַח “in security”, with יָשַׁב or שָׁכַן “dwell” or שָׁכַב “lie down”. The security is either Yahweh's gift, chiefly to Israel in the land, or the ease of those who do not see danger coming.

senses.definition: Safety without fear of enemy or beast, given by Yahweh: Israel dwelling in the land under his covenant, and the one who lies down in peace because Yahweh keeps him.

evidence.note: “Do my statutes … and you will dwell on the land in security (לָבֶטַח); the land will give its fruit and you will eat your fill and dwell in security upon it.”
“You will dwell in security in your land; I will give peace in the land, and you will lie down and none will make you afraid.”
“Israel dwells in security, alone, the fountain of Jacob, in a land of grain and wine.”
“When he gives you rest from all your enemies around, and you dwell in security.”
“Judah and Israel dwelt in security, each man under his vine and under his fig tree, from Dan to Beersheba, all the days of Solomon.”
“In peace I will lie down and sleep, for you alone, Yahweh, make me dwell in security.”
“My flesh also will dwell in security”: quoted in Act 2:26 as resting “in hope”.
“Whoever listens to me will dwell in security and be at ease from dread of evil.”
“Then you will walk your way in security, and your foot will not stumble.”
“The needy will lie down in security.”
“The work of righteousness will be peace, and the service of righteousness quietness and security forever.”
In the days of the righteous Branch of David “Judah will be saved and Israel will dwell in security”.
“I will gather them from all the lands … and make them dwell in security.”
A covenant of peace under “my servant David”: “they will dwell in the wilderness in security and sleep in the forests … and none will make them afraid.”
“When they dwell in security on their land and none makes them afraid.”
“I will break bow and sword and war from the land, and make them lie down in security.”
“There will be no more curse; Jerusalem will dwell in security.”
“He led them in security and they did not fear, but the sea covered their enemies.”
“He who walks in integrity walks securely.”

senses.definition: The ease of a people or city that does not expect attack, or that thinks itself beyond harm; the security of the proud before judgment.

evidence.note: Simeon and Levi “came upon the city בֶּטַח and killed every male”: the men were in pain and expected nothing.
Gideon “struck the camp, and the camp was בֶטַח”: off guard.
Laish “dwelling in security, quiet and secure”.
Babylon, “you who dwell in security, who say in your heart, I am, and there is none besides me”.
Nineveh, “the exultant city that dwelt in security … how it has become a desolation”.
Messengers go out “to terrify Cush in its security”.
Fire on Magog “and on those who dwell in security in the coastlands”.
“A nation at ease that dwells in security, with no gates or bars, dwelling alone.”
“You strip the robe from those who pass by unsuspecting (בֶּטַח), like men returning from war.”
“Do not devise evil against your neighbour while he dwells in security beside you.”
God gives the oppressor security, “and he is supported, but his eyes are on their ways”.
Israel regathered “dwelling in security, all of them” when Gog comes.
Gog: “I will go up against the land of open villages, against the quiet who dwell in security, all of them dwelling without walls, and having no bars or gates.”

evidence.locator: Psa.4.9; Psa.16.9; Jdg.18.7; Hos.2.20; Zep.2.15, בֶּטַח → ἐλπίδι; ἐλπίς renders בֶּטַח ×9, and מִבְטָח (Psa.40.5; Jer.17.7) and בִּטָּחוֹן (Ecc.9.4)

evidence.note: Peter quotes Psa 16:9, “my flesh also will rest in hope (ἐπ᾽ ἐλπίδι)”, the Septuagint's words for לָבֶטַח, and expounds it of Christ's resurrection (Act 2:29–31).

evidence.locator: Ezk.38.8, 11, 14, לָבֶטַח → ἐν εἰρήνῃ / εἰρήνης; εἰρήνη renders בֶּטַח ×6

evidence.note: “When they say, Peace and safety (εἰρήνη καὶ ἀσφάλεια), then sudden destruction comes on them”: the false security of the unsuspecting sense.

parallels.note: Peace: “in peace I will lie down … you make me dwell in security”.
Alone, apart: the security of a people on its own.

opposites.note: “None will make them afraid (וְאֵין מַחֲרִיד)”, the common close of dwelling in security.

senses.definition: The person or thing on which one's trust rests: Yahweh for those who trust him, or a false god, a foreign ally, gold or a spider's web for the rest.

evidence.note: “Blessed is the man who trusts in Yahweh, and Yahweh is his מִבְטָח.”
“Happy is the man who makes Yahweh his מִבְטָח, and does not turn to the proud.”
“You are my hope, Lord Yahweh, my מִבְטָח from my youth.”
“God of our salvation, the confidence of all the ends of the earth.”
“That your trust may be in Yahweh.”
“As the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel, their מִבְטָח.”
“Yahweh has rejected those in whom you trust.”
Egypt will no more be “the confidence of the house of Israel”.
“If I have made gold my hope, or called fine gold my מִבְטָח.”
The godless man's “trust is a spider's house”.
“Confidence in a faithless man in the day of trouble is a broken tooth and a slipping foot.”
The wise brings down “the stronghold in which it trusts”.

senses.definition: The state of being secure, or the place where one is secure.

evidence.note: “My people will dwell in a peaceful habitation, in secure dwellings (מִבְטַחִים), in quiet resting places.”
“In the fear of Yahweh is strong confidence, and his children will have a refuge.”
The wicked man is torn “from his tent, his security”.

words.summary: Three uses: twice the Rabshakeh's taunt, once the hope that belongs only to the living.

senses.definition: That on which one rests one's confidence.

evidence.note: “What is this confidence (הַבִּטָּחוֹן) in which you trust (בָּטָחְתָּ)?”

senses.definition: Ground for expecting good, which the living have and the dead do not.

evidence.note: “Whoever is joined to all the living has בִּטָּחוֹן, for a living dog is better than a dead lion. For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing.”

words.summary: Once, in Isa 30:15; its sense rests on that verse and on the verb.

senses.definition: Trust in Yahweh that waits quietly, instead of running to Egypt for help.

evidence.note: “In returning and rest you will be saved; in quietness and in trust (בְּהַשְׁקֵט וּבְבִטְחָה) will be your strength. But you would not”: set against the flight to Egypt (Isa 30:2, 16).

words.summary: Once, plural, in Job 12:6; its sense rests on that verse and on the noun בֶּטַח.

senses.definition: Security enjoyed by those who provoke God.

evidence.note: “The tents of robbers prosper, and there is security (וּבַטֻּחוֹת) for those who provoke God”: parallel to יִשְׁלָיוּ “are at ease”.

words.summary: A city of Hadadezer king of Zobah from which David took much bronze. The parallel in 1Ch 18:8 reads טִבְחַת, Tibhath, with the first two letters in the other order, so the spelling is uncertain. The name is spelled as the noun “security”, but scripture does not explain it. Nothing ties the name to the root's sense beyond its spelling, so the root's cognates count against it. A place, so it has no name entry.

senses.definition: A city of Hadadezer king of Zobah.

evidence.note: “From Betah (וּמִבֶּטַח) and from Berothai, cities of Hadadezer, King David took very much bronze.”
The parallel: “from Tibhath and from Cun”.

words.summary: Once, plural אֲבַטִּחִים, among the foods Israel remembered from Egypt. A separate word in the same spelling: the Arabic shows ḫ behind ח where the trust root's only Arabic candidate shows ḥ, and no link to “trust” is known. The word for the fruit is shared by Aramaic and Arabic and may have travelled with the fruit.

senses.definition: A fruit of Egypt, named with cucumbers, leeks, onions and garlic.

evidence.note: “We remember the fish we ate in Egypt for nothing, the cucumbers and the watermelons (הָאֲבַטִּחִים), the leeks, the onions and the garlic.”

cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic of the Talmud and Targums: both sides of the Hebrew, trusting (“since he trusts in idols”) and feeling secure; the Targum of Jer 12:5 uses the ithpeel for the Hebrew qal “if in a land of peace you are secure”.

evidence.locator: s.v. בְּטַח (ch.), citing Taan. 22b (trusts in idols); Af. Targ. Ruth II, 13; Ithpe. Targ. Jer. XII, 5 (to feel safe)

cognates.note: Punic bṭḥ “trust”, listed with the Aramaic and Hebrew verb under one Proto-Semitic set. Not yet followed to the inscriptions.

evidence.locator: SEM000986 bṭḥ [trust] V, PUN000315 bṭḥ [trust] V; ARM003679 BṬḤ [trust] V

cognates.gloss: spread out; throw down on his face; (VII) lie stretched out on the ground
cognates.note: If this is the same root, the picture is lying stretched out on the ground, as the Hebrew “lie down in security” (Psa 4:9; Hos 2:20; Job 11:18); Arabic has no “trust” here, so it is argued, not shown. It would put ḥ behind ח.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 216, art. بطح, بَطَحَهُ (n2734)
evidence.note: “He spread it; spread it out … He threw him down upon his face.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 216, art. بطح, انبطح (n2737)
evidence.note: “He lay, or lay as though thrown down or extended, upon his face … extended upon the ground.”

cognates.note: The same fruit name as אֲבַטִּיחַ, with ḫ behind ח: a different older consonant from the ḥ of بطح. Being the name of a traded fruit, it may have passed between the languages rather than descended in each.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 216, art. بطخ, بِطِّيخٌ (n2750)
evidence.note: “A certain well-known fruit; the melon, absolutely … and, particularly, the water-melon.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 216, art. بطخ, أَبْطَخُوا (n2746)
evidence.note: “They had abundance of بِطِّيخ.”

cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic; Targum Onkelos renders the אֲבַטִּחִים of Num 11:5 by its plural.

evidence.locator: s.v. אֲבַטִּיחָא (ch.), citing Targ. O. Num. XI, 5; and s.v. אֲבַטִּיחַ, melon, Maasr. I, 4–5

doctrine.statement: Scripture sets two objects of trust against each other: “Cursed is the man who trusts in man and makes flesh his arm … blessed is the man who trusts in Yahweh” (Jer 17:5–7); “better to take refuge in Yahweh than to trust in man” (Psa 118:8–9). The reason given is that man dies: “Do not trust in princes, in a son of man, in whom there is no salvation. His breath goes out, he returns to his earth; in that very day his thoughts perish” (Psa 146:3–4). Those who trust in wealth cannot redeem a brother from death; wise and foolish alike die, and man in honour without understanding “is like the beasts that perish” (Psa 49:7–13, 21). A man's own righteousness is no ground either (Ezk 33:13), and Paul learned “not to trust in ourselves but in God who raises the dead” (2Co 1:9). From the verses: man has no life in himself to save himself or another; the only sure trust is in Yahweh, who alone can raise the dead.

“Whoever is joined to all the living has hope (בִּטָּחוֹן), for a living dog is better than a dead lion. For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing, and they have no more reward … there is no work or thought or knowledge or wisdom in the grave, where you are going” (Ecc 9:4–5, 10). From the verses: hope belongs to the living; the dead are without knowledge, and death is not a passage to conscious life elsewhere.

David wrote, “my flesh also will dwell in security (לָבֶטַח), for you will not abandon my soul to the grave, nor let your holy one see corruption” (Psa 16:9–10). Peter quotes it, “my flesh also will rest in hope”, and argues that David “both died and was buried, and his tomb is with us to this day”, so that David spoke of the resurrection of the Christ, whose flesh did not see corruption (Act 2:26–31); Paul argues the same (Act 13:35–37). From the verses: the flesh that lies in the grave rests secure only in the hope of resurrection; David himself is still in the grave, and Christ was raised.

Dwelling “in security” on the land is the promised blessing of keeping Yahweh's covenant (Lev 25:18–19; 26:5–6), briefly tasted under Solomon, “each man under his vine and under his fig tree” (1Ki 5:5). The prophets place its fulfilment in the days of the righteous Branch raised to David: “in his days Judah will be saved and Israel will dwell in security” (Jer 23:5–6; 33:15–16); Yahweh will gather them “from all the lands” and make them dwell in security (Jer 32:37), under “my servant David” as shepherd with a covenant of peace (Ezk 34:23–28), and Jerusalem “will dwell in security” with no more curse when Yahweh is king over all the earth (Zec 14:9, 11). From the verses: the security of Israel in the land is part of the kingdom the Son of David will set up on earth, still future, in the land promised to the fathers.

Gog is mustered “in the latter years” against “a land brought back from the sword, gathered from many peoples, on the mountains of Israel”, whose people “dwell in security, all of them” (Ezk 38:8). He says, “I will go up against the land of open villages, against the quiet who dwell in security, all of them without walls” (Ezk 38:11), and comes “from your place in the far north” when “my people Israel dwell in security” (Ezk 38:14–16). Yahweh destroys him on the mountains of Israel and sends fire on those “who dwell in security in the coastlands” (Ezk 39:2–6), and afterward Israel dwells “in security on their land, and none makes them afraid” (Ezk 39:26–28). From the verses: Israel is first regathered to its land and living there without walls, then a power from the far north invades it in the latter days, and Yahweh's own intervention ends that invasion and brings in Israel's lasting security.

note: Words: takes b.bi.aa (verb, including the passive participle בָּטוּחַ, Isa 26:3; Psa 112:7), b.bi.ab, b.bi.af with the zero-token cross-reference m.ai.ap, b.bi.ad, b.bi.ac, b.bi.ae, b.bi.ag (Betah, a place, kept as a word; no name entry), and b.bj.ab with the zero-token a.ag.ac (אֲבַטִּיחַ). No personal names are formed from the root. Open questions: (1) The root's basic picture is not shown by a cognate: the only Arabic candidate, بطح “throw down on the face, lie stretched out”, is recorded as possible; Jewish Aramaic and Punic share the meaning “trust” but not an older picture. Old Canaanite ba-ṭi-i-ti (“I am secure”, Amarna EA 147:56) is reported in the leads and not yet followed to an edition. Ugaritic and Ge'ez not yet checked. (2) אֲבַטִּיחַ is a separate word (Arabic ḫ, against ḥ in بطح); Syriac ܦܛܝܚܐ paṭṭīḥā “melon” (Wiktionary; to be checked in Payne Smith) has p, and Wiktionary reports a proposed Egyptian bddw-kꜣ origin, not checked in the TLA. (3) Betah (2Sa 8:8) is Tibhath (טִבְחַת) in 1Ch 18:8: which order is original is not settled. The Peshitta does not use a cognate root for “trust” (it uses ܬܟܠ), so there is no Syriac word of the entry. The Septuagint's ἐλπίς for לָבֶטַח in Psa 16:9 is what Act 2:26 quotes.
